subject: Finishes that help a workspace feel calm
hook: The quietest finish starts at the edge bander
ig:
The quietest finish starts at the edge bander.

This is how we work on every panel that ends up as a desk, shelf or door. A freshly cut board has a raw edge. On a calm, matt home office wall, a raw or mismatched edge is the thing your eye keeps finding.

So each visible edge goes through our edge bander: colour-matched ABS edging is applied, trimmed flush and the corners cleaned. The result is a door or shelf that reads as one solid colour rather than a face with an outline.

We choose the edge thickness for the job: thinner on internal shelves, thicker where knees, chairs and bags knock against the front of a desk.

It's not glamorous, but it's the difference between furniture that looks calm across the room and furniture that looks calm up close too.

Want to see edged samples in the finish you're considering? Send us a DM and we'll arrange it.
fb:
Thirty seconds from our Hanley workshop: how a matt panel gets its clean edge.

Every visible edge on our furniture runs through the edge bander, where colour-matched ABS edging is applied and trimmed flush. It's a small step, but it's why a matt desk or cupboard front looks like one quiet block of colour instead of a panel with a line around it. On a home office wall you look at every day, that matters more than you'd think.

If you're planning a workspace and want to see edged samples in person, drop us a message or take a look at how we work here:
